chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Munqari, from Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).

A man came to him and asked him, saying: 'What is abstinence (al-zuhd)?' He said: 'Abstinence is ten parts. The highest rank of abstinence is the lowest rank of piety (al-wara'), and the highest rank of piety is the lowest rank of certitude (al-yaqin), and the highest rank of certitude is the lowest rank of contentment (al-rida). And indeed, abstinence is summarized in one verse of God's Book, the Mighty and Glorious: "In order that you may not despair over what passes you by, nor exult over what He has given you."'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Contentment or satisfaction with divine decree
key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: Piety or God-consciousness, specifically avoiding doubtful matters
key_terms.لِكَيْلَا تَأْسَوْا: In order that you may not despair

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of spiritual abstinence (Zuhd) in Shia hadith and how does it relate to Quranic verses?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) elucidates the spiritual hierarchy of *zuhd* (asceticism), tracing its roots from the highest degree of piety (*wara'*) down to the foundational state of contentment (*rida*). By anchoring this definition in Surah Al-Hadid, he highlights that true detachment is not merely renunciation of the world, but an internal equilibrium of the heart that prevents emotional extremes of despair and arrogance. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on inner purification (*tazkiyah*) as the prerequisite for spiritual certainty (*yaqin*).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-26 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Munqeri, on the authority of Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB) ,

“A man went to see Imam As-Sajjad (MGB) and asked, ‘What is abstinence?’ Imam As-Sajjad (MGB) said, "There are ten ranks of abstinence. The highest rank of abstinence is the lowest rank of piety. The highest rank of piety is the lowest rank of certitude. The highest rank of certitude is the lowest rank of contentment, and all abstinence is summarized in just one of the verses of God’s Book: ‘In order that ye may not despair over matters that pass by you, nor exult over the favors bestowed upon you. ’”
